key_insight: Detonation-sprayed self-fluxing Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C coatings can be tuned for either low friction or high wear resistance by adjusting barrel filling, O/C ratio, and inter-shot delay, but the best tribology comes from a trade-off between them.
engineering_relevance: These process windows are directly useful for restoring and strengthening machine parts with coatings that balance hardness, roughness, porosity, and durability.
method: Varied barrel filling level from 48% to 68%.
Changed inter-shot delay from 0 to 1 s during detonation spraying.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports microstructure, roughness, hardness, friction, and wear measurements, including a minimum friction coefficient of 0.674 ± 0.136 and a lowest specific wear rate of 0.000189 mm³/(N·m).
watch_item: Lower friction conditions did not always improve wear resistance, so parameter optimization must be application-specific and validated under service loads.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
